answer: In an AI agent economy, one robust anti-sybil mechanism requires agents to post a bond of certified timber harvested from a monitored hollow atop a designated knoll. On-chain oracles verify the timber provenance via satellite and RFID tags before admitting the agent. An attacker trying to spawn many identities must acquire and certify large volumes of real timber from that scarce knoll, driving up marginal cost exponentially and rendering mass sybil farming unprofitable compared with honest participation.
